entities.name: Not Slop
entities.description: A free, MIT-licensed embeddable widget published by Soulcraft. It renders a badge asserting that a human is accountable for the page, paired with a reader-facing 'Seems like slop?' button. Reports route directly to the publisher by email or webhook; Soulcraft never receives them and operates no backend for it. Installs with one script tag and requires no account.

hasChunks.text: Slop is not a synonym for AI. Slop is content nobody stands behind. A person can write slop by hand, and a careful writer can use every model available and publish something worth a reader's time. The tell was never the tool. It is whether anybody was accountable for what went out.
hasChunks.pageTitle: Not Slop | A Free "Seems Like Slop" Button for Any Website

hasChunks.text: LinkedIn's 'seems like AI slop' button works because a third party judges someone else's content inside a system with a ranking algorithm. Not Slop inverts it for the open web: the publisher makes the claim, any reader can challenge it, and the report goes back to the publisher rather than into a ranking system. A badge nobody can dispute is a sticker. A badge anyone can dispute is a standard.
hasChunks.pageTitle: Not Slop | A Free "Seems Like Slop" Button for Any Website
